brief.headline: Russia claims Konstantinovka, hits Kyiv; Ukraine drones reach Omsk
brief.lead: Pro-Kremlin channels celebrated the claimed capture of Konstantinovka and overnight strikes on Kyiv's defense industry, but sentiment split sharply as Ukraine's 625-drone barrage reached Omsk 2,500km away and battered Crimea, fueling unusually blunt self-criticism of Russian air defense.

developments.title: Channels claim full Russian control of Konstantinovka
developments.body: Multiple channels declared Konstantinovka (Donetsk) liberated, citing captured Ukrainian soldiers 'confirming' Russian control and 'thanking' captors — an unconfirmed framing. Poddubny reported over a thousand civilians may remain and DPR readied evacuation centers.

developments.title: Overnight strikes hit Kyiv defense plants, ammunition depots
developments.body: Channels claimed combined missile/drone strikes damaged Kyiv defense plants (naming Vizar and 'Kyiv-71/1/79'), a Patriot ammunition depot near Vishnyove, and energy infrastructure, citing secondary detonations. Claims are channel-sourced and unverified; Rybar said the Vizar hit caused no nuclear contamination.

developments.title: Ukraine's 625-drone barrage reaches Omsk refinery 2,500km away
developments.body: Channels reported Ukraine launched 625 long-range drones (Russia claiming 613 intercepted), striking for the first time the Omsk refinery ~2,500km from the border and hitting Leningrad, Yaroslavl and Moscow regions. Rybar tied Leningrad strikes to Finnish airspace restrictions.

developments.title: Crimea energy, ferries and Kursk NPP cooling tower struck
developments.body: Channels reported systematic Ukrainian strikes isolating Crimea — energy, fuel and ferry infrastructure in Sevastopol and Kherson — and claimed a drone struck a Kursk nuclear plant cooling tower with detections near Leningrad and Smolensk reactors. Two Majors also cited attacks on Azov Sea fuel tankers.

developments.title: Azerbaijan-Russia friction over SOCAR fuel station strike
developments.body: Channels reported Azerbaijan protesting the Russian strike on a SOCAR fuel station in Ukraine as deliberate targeting and discrimination; Starshe Eddy criticized the Foreign Ministry's inaction — a rare elite-tension signal within pro-war coverage.

developments.title: SVR blames British intelligence for Sevastopol museum strike
developments.body: Several channels amplified an SVR claim that British intelligence orchestrated the Ukrainian drone strike on Sevastopol's Panorama/Defense Museum — an unverified attribution shifting blame to Western handlers.

narrative_watch.title: Blunt self-criticism of Russian air defense
narrative_watch.body: After Omsk and Crimea strikes, channels openly argued Russian air defense is inadequate against cheap mass drone/missile attacks across vast territory — unusually candid for pro-war outlets.

narrative_watch.title: 'Dying Ukrainian regime' frame
narrative_watch.body: Poddubny and Kotsnews framed the Konstantinovka claim as proof of Russia's superior military, economy and society versus a collapsing, externally-dependent Ukraine.

narrative_watch.title: Strikes 'justified' by human-shield claims
narrative_watch.body: Channels repeatedly claimed Ukrainian weapons and munitions (including alleged depleted-uranium and cluster stocks) sit in residential areas, pre-justifying Russian deep strikes.

mood_lines.text: Uniformly triumphant (net +100); channels claim precise, intelligence-driven hits on Kyiv defense plants, depots and fuel infrastructure with secondary detonations.
Confident (net +100), dominated by the Konstantinovka capture claim and reported advances near Volchansk, Sumy, Zaporizhzhia and Krasnyi Liman.
Sharply negative (net -62, worsening); the 625-drone barrage, Omsk refinery hit and Crimea/Kursk NPP strikes drove alarm and defensive framing.
Negative (net -33); focus on Polish PAC-3 aid scandal, Norway missile dispute, Vance's 'exhausted Russia' remark and Romanian naval drones.
Split to neutral (net 0, mood down 29); Azerbaijan SOCAR row, migrant symbol case and Omsk fire offset FSB and Duma nomination positives.
Fully negative (net -100); jabs at Foreign Ministry inaction and Zelensky, but no direct Putin criticism this cycle.

flag_texts.title: Ukraine strikes on Russia mood worsens (+38 toward negative)
flag_texts.body: The 21 posts on Ukrainian strikes swung to net -62 as channels absorbed the record 625-drone barrage, the first Omsk refinery hit 2,500km away, and Crimea/Kursk NPP strikes — with several openly conceding air-defense gaps.

flag_texts.title: West & NATO sentiment sours (move 29)
flag_texts.body: West coverage dropped to net -33, driven by Poland's PAC-3 aid scandal, a Norway missile-funding dispute, Vance signaling Russia's offensive is 'nearly exhausted,' and Romanian US-made naval drones in the Black Sea.

flag_texts.title: Russia internal mood declines (move -29)
flag_texts.body: Domestic sentiment fell to net 0 amid the Azerbaijan SOCAR protest, a leniently-fined migrant wearing Ukrainian symbols, and drone debris causing a fire in Omsk — partly offset by an FSB explosives-plot bust.

flag_texts.title: Watchlist topics quiet: mobilisation, Putin criticism
flag_texts.body: No posts touched mobilisation rumours or direct criticism of Putin this cycle; the criticism that appeared targeted the Foreign Ministry and Zelensky, not the Kremlin leadership.
